g.text: The physical layer conduits transporting raw electromagnetic or optical signals between network interfaces.
Principle: Pairs of insulated copper conductors twisted together. Cancels EMI and crosstalk
via differential signaling (equal & opposite voltages on each wire in pair).
Cat6 / Cat6a: 250 / 500 MHz, 10 Gbps (Cat6 to 55m; Cat6a to 100m with spline)
Cat8: 2 GHz, 25G / 40G Base-T up to 30m (Top-of-Rack datacenter switching)
Connector: 8P8C (RJ45 modular jack). Shielded STP adds foil shield around pairs.
Construction: Solid central copper core, dielectric insulator, braided metallic shield,
and outer PVC protective jacket. Shield blocks outer RF noise and contains inner emission.
75Ω Broadband: RG-6 / RG-59 (Cable TV, DOCSIS 3.1 / 4.0 Gigabit Cable Modems)
Connectors: BNC (bayonet lock), F-type (threaded screw connector for TV/DOCSIS)
Physics: Total Internal Reflection (TIR) through ultra-pure silica glass core enclosed
by a lower refractive index cladding (n₁ > n₂). 100% immune to EMI, RFI, and EMP.
Single-Mode Fiber (SMF - Yellow): ~9µm tiny core, 1310/1550nm laser light.
Zero modal dispersion. Reaches 10 km to 100+ km without repeaters. Subsea & Telco WAN.
Multi-Mode Fiber (MMF - Aqua/Orange): 50 / 62.5µm wide core, 850nm VCSEL.
Modal dispersion bounces light rays along multiple paths. Max 300m - 550m. Datacenter LAN.
Connectors: LC (compact duplex), SC (push-pull), ST (twist), MPO/MTP (12-24 fibers)
Coverage: Personal Area Networks, low power consumption, wearable/peripheral interconnect.
Employs frequency hopping and spread spectrum modulation to mitigate RF interference.
Bluetooth / BLE (802.15.1): 2.4 GHz ISM, 1–3 Mbps (up to 2 Mbps BLE 5), 10–100m
NFC (Near Field): 13.56 MHz, 424 kbps, < 4 cm (Apple Pay, Google Wallet, smart badges)
Zigbee & Thread (802.15.4): 2.4 GHz mesh networking for smart home IoT sensor nodes
Infrared (IrDA): Line-of-sight optical pulse (300 GHz – 400 THz), TV remotes
Mechanism: Radio waves with CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance).
OFDMA and Multi-User MIMO (MU-MIMO) transmit to multiple clients concurrently.
2.4 GHz Band: Long range, high wall penetration, 3 non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 11)
5 GHz Band (Wi-Fi 5/6): Higher bandwidth, lower latency, up to 160 MHz channel width
6 GHz Band (Wi-Fi 6E / Wi-Fi 7): 320 MHz ultra-wide channels, up to 46 Gbps theoretical
Cellular: Hexagonal geographic cell towers handling handoffs, licensed spectrum (3GPP).
Satellite: Microwave space links bridging remote terrains and transoceanic flights.
4G LTE / LTE-A: All-IP packet switched network, 100–300 Mbps, 30–50ms latency
5G NR (New Radio): Sub-6 GHz + mmWave (24–40 GHz), beamforming, < 5ms URLLC
LEO Satellite (Starlink): ~550 km orbit, 100–250 Mbps, 25–45ms low latency
GEO Satellite (Legacy): 35,786 km geostationary orbit, 500–650ms high latency
Bands: Ka-band (26-40 GHz), Ku-band (12-18 GHz), C-band (4-8 GHz)
